title: CBSE Class 12 Business Studies · Practice paper 1
subject: Business Studies
label: Practice paper
instr: This question paper contains 34 questions. All questions are compulsory.
Marks are indicated against each question.
Answers should be brief and to the point.
Answers to the questions carrying 3 marks may be from 50 to 75 words.
Answers to the questions carrying 4 marks may be about 150 words.
Answers to the questions carrying 6 marks may be about 200 words.
Attempt all parts of the questions together.

The board paper numbers the questions 1 to 34 without sections. Here they are grouped by marks:
Section A: questions 1 to 20 (1 mark each)
Section B: questions 21 to 24 (3 marks each)
Section C: questions 25 to 30 (4 marks each)
Section D: questions 31 to 34 (6 marks each)
Internal choices of the board paper are not included: each question has one version.
This is a practice paper written in the pattern of the CBSE Sample Question Paper 2026-27. It is not an official CBSE paper.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: Mr Anand is the Production Manager of a company. He reports to the Chief Executive Officer and has several supervisors working under him. Identify the function that he will perform at the level at which he is working.
options: Formulating the overall organisational goals and strategies.
Directly overseeing the efforts of the workers on the shop floor.
Being responsible for the welfare and survival of the organisation.
Interpreting the policies framed by top management and assigning duties to supervisors.
questions.sol: As Production Manager between the CEO and the supervisors, Mr Anand is at the middle level. Middle-level managers interpret the policies framed by top management and assign necessary duties and responsibilities to supervisors. Goals, strategies and survival of the organisation are top-level tasks; overseeing workers is a supervisory task.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: In a garment factory, the output of the workers fell sharply in the last two hours of every shift. An expert was asked to determine the amount and frequency of rest intervals the workers need to regain their energy. Name the technique of Scientific Management being used.
questions.sol: Fatigue study seeks to determine the amount and frequency of rest intervals needed to complete a task, so that workers can regain lost stamina and keep up their efficiency.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: Which of the following statements about informal organisation is correct?
options: It is deliberately designed by management to achieve organisational goals.
It clearly defines the authority and responsibility of every member.
It arises from the interaction of people at work and has no written rules.
Communication in it flows only through the scalar chain.
questions.sol: Informal organisation emerges on its own from the social interaction of people working together. It has no written rules, and communication does not follow a planned path. The other three statements describe formal organisation.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text:
Read the following statements carefully:
Statement I: Apprenticeship training puts the trainee under the guidance of a master worker.
Statement II: Development is a job-oriented process that improves the skills of an employee for doing a particular job.
Choose the correct option from the following:
options: Statement I is true and Statement II is false.
Statement II is true and Statement I is false.
questions.sol: Statement I is true: in apprenticeship training the trainee works under a master worker. Statement II is false: it describes training. Development is a career-oriented process aimed at the overall growth of the employee.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: Netra Opticals, a chain of spectacle shops, noticed early that young customers were beginning to buy spectacles online. Before any of its rivals, it launched its own mobile app with a virtual try-on feature and won a large share of the online customers. Identify the importance of understanding the business environment highlighted above.
options: It helps in tapping useful resources.
It helps the firm to identify threats and early warning signals.
It enables the firm to identify opportunities and get the first mover advantage.
questions.sol: By sensing the change in customer buying habits early and acting before its rivals, the firm identified an opportunity and gained the first mover advantage.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: Choose the correct statement about the controlling function of management:
options: Controlling is required only in large business organisations.
Controlling is a pervasive function performed by managers at all levels and in all types of organisations.
Controlling is only a backward-looking function.
Controlling ensures that deviations from standards never occur.
questions.sol: Controlling is a pervasive function: it is performed at all levels of management and in all types of organisations, large or small, business or non-business. It is both backward-looking and forward-looking, and it cannot prevent all deviations; it finds them and corrects them.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text:
Match the terms in Column 1 with their meanings in Column 2:
Column 1Column 2
1. Money market(i) An institution that holds the securities of investors in electronic form
2. Secondary market(ii) A market for the buying and selling of existing securities
3. Depository(iii) A market for short-term funds with a maturity of up to one year
4. Stock exchange(iv) A body that assists, regulates and controls the business of buying, selling and dealing in securities
Choose the correct option from the following:
questions.sol: The money market deals in short-term funds of up to one year; the secondary market is where existing securities are traded; a depository holds securities in electronic form; and a stock exchange is the body that assists, regulates and controls dealing in securities.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: Who among the following cannot file a complaint under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019?
options: The Central Government or any State Government
A wholesaler who bought the goods for resale
The legal heir of a deceased consumer
questions.sol: A person who buys goods for resale or for a commercial purpose is not a consumer under the Act, so the wholesaler cannot file a complaint as a consumer. A consumer, a registered consumers' association, the Central or a State Government and the legal heir or representative of a deceased consumer can file a complaint.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: In Sudha Foods Ltd., Kavya, a supervisor in the Production Department, has to inform Rohit, a supervisor at the same level in the Sales Department, about an urgent change in the delivery schedule. Passing the message up and down through the departmental heads would cause delay, so with the prior permission of their superiors she contacts Rohit directly. This arrangement is provided for under which principle of management?
questions.sol: Under Fayol's principle of scalar chain, communication normally follows the formal line of authority. In an emergency, employees at the same level may contact each other directly through a 'gang plank' with the permission of their superiors, so that the chain is not violated and delay is avoided.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text:
Assertion (A): Labelling helps in the promotion of a product.
Reason (R): A carefully designed label can attract the attention of buyers and give them reasons to buy the product.
Choose the correct option:
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.sol: Both statements are true. Promotion of the product is one of the functions of a label, and it is performed precisely because an attractive, well-designed label draws attention and gives reasons for purchase. So R correctly explains A.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: Meena bought a mixer-grinder from a local shop and did not take a bill, to save time. When the mixer stopped working within a week, the shopkeeper refused to accept that it had been bought from his shop. Which consumer responsibility did Meena ignore?
options: Read labels carefully to know about price, net weight and the dates of manufacture and expiry.
Buy only standardised goods, as they give an assurance of quality.
Ask for a cash memo on the purchase of goods or services.
Learn about the risks associated with products and services.
questions.sol: A cash memo is the proof of purchase. Without it Meena cannot easily prove that she bought the mixer from that shop, which she would need to do to get it repaired or replaced or to file a complaint.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: Which of the following statements about the financing decision is correct?
options: Issue of more debt dilutes the control of the existing equity shareholders.
Debt is generally a cheaper source of finance than equity, but it is riskier for the business.
Equity share capital involves a fixed obligation to pay dividend every year.
Floatation costs have no effect on the choice of the source of finance.
questions.sol: Interest on debt is usually lower than the return expected by equity shareholders and is tax-deductible, so debt is cheaper. But interest and repayment of principal are obligatory, so debt increases financial risk. Debt does not dilute control, equity has no fixed dividend obligation, and floatation costs do affect the choice.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: SEBI prohibits insider trading and fraudulent and unfair trade practices in the securities market. Under which category of SEBI's functions do these fall?
questions.sol: Prohibiting fraudulent and unfair trade practices, controlling insider trading and taking steps to protect investors are protective functions of SEBI.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: A notice in a factory reads: 'Smoking is not allowed inside the factory premises. Any worker found smoking will be fined ₹500.' Identify the type of plan.
questions.sol: A rule is a specific statement that tells what must or must not be done, with no flexibility or discretion. Violation usually carries a penalty, as here.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a capital budgeting (investment) decision?
options: Deciding how much cash to keep for day-to-day expenses
Deciding the credit period to be allowed to customers
Purchasing a new machine with a working life of ten years
Deciding the rate of dividend to be paid this year
questions.sol: Capital budgeting decisions are long-term investment decisions about fixed assets, such as buying a machine that will be used for ten years. Cash and credit decisions are working capital decisions; the rate of dividend is a dividend decision.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: During a festival month, a detergent brand offered 'Buy two packs, get one free' to boost its immediate sales. Identify the element of the promotion mix used.
questions.sol: Sales promotion consists of short-term incentives, such as offering extra quantity free, that encourage immediate purchase of a product.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: An umbrella manufacturer needs much more money to buy raw materials and hold stock in the months before the monsoon than at other times of the year. Identify the factor affecting its working capital requirement.
questions.sol: Umbrellas sell mainly in the rainy season. During the peak season the level of activity is higher, so more working capital is required; in the lean season less is needed. This is the effect of seasonal factors.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: Greenleaf Ltd. makes snacks. It studies what customers want, uses biodegradable packaging and has reduced the salt and fat in its products, so that it satisfies its customers while also caring for the long-term welfare of society. Which marketing philosophy does Greenleaf Ltd. follow?
questions.sol: The societal marketing concept aims at satisfying the needs of customers while also taking care of the long-term welfare of society, for example by protecting the environment and the health of consumers.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: A company has 1,00,000 equity shares of ₹10 each and ₹20,00,000 of 10% debentures. Its earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) are ₹6,00,000 and the tax rate is 40%. What is its earnings per share (EPS)?

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: A software firm redesigned the jobs of its programmers so that they handle more challenging work, with greater autonomy and more opportunity for personal growth. Identify the incentive used.
questions.sol: Job enrichment means designing jobs to include greater variety of work content, a higher level of knowledge and skill, more autonomy and responsibility, and opportunity for personal growth. It is a non-financial incentive.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text:
Zenith Ltd. fills every vacancy above the entry level only by promoting or transferring its own employees. It never advertises these posts outside the company.
State any three limitations of the source of recruitment followed by Zenith Ltd.
questions.model:
Zenith Ltd. uses internal sources of recruitment. Their limitations (any three):
1. The scope for induction of fresh talent is reduced, as people with new ideas and skills from outside do not get a chance.
2. Employees may become lethargic if they are sure of time-bound promotions.
3. The spirit of competition among the employees may be hampered.
4. Frequent transfers of employees may often reduce the productivity of the organisation.
5. A new enterprise cannot use internal sources of recruitment, as no one can be recruited from within.

points.t: First limitation correctly stated (any one from the model answer)
Second limitation correctly stated (any one from the model answer)
Third limitation correctly stated (any one from the model answer)

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: In Vatsal Textiles, the news that the company might close one of its units spread within a few hours among the workers through casual talks in the canteen and at the factory gate. By the time it reached the night shift, the story had changed to 'all the workers will lose their jobs', and nobody could tell where the news had started. Some workers stopped working, and the Production Manager had to call a meeting to explain the real position.

parts.q: (a) Identify the type of communication through which the news spread.

points.t: Informal communication / grapevine

parts.q: (b) State any two features of this type of communication highlighted in the case.
parts.model:
Features of informal communication highlighted (any two):
1. It spreads very fast: 'spread within a few hours among the workers'.
2. It often gets distorted: 'the story had changed to all the workers will lose their jobs'.
3. It is difficult to detect its source: 'nobody could tell where the news had started'.
4. It arises out of social interaction and does not follow the official channels: 'casual talks in the canteen and at the factory gate'.

points.t: First feature correctly stated, matching the case (any one from the model answer)
Second feature correctly stated, matching the case (any one from the model answer)

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text:
Explain the following factors affecting the dividend decision of a company:
(a) Stability of earnings
(b) Taxation policy
questions.model:
(a) Stability of earnings: A company having stable earnings is in a better position to declare higher dividends. A company having unstable (fluctuating) earnings is likely to pay smaller dividends, so that it can keep up its payments in bad years.
(b) Taxation policy: The choice between paying dividends and retaining earnings is affected by how dividends are taxed. If the tax on dividends is higher, it is better to pay less by way of dividends. If the tax rate is relatively lower, higher dividends may be declared.

points.t: (a) A company with stable earnings can declare higher dividends
(a) A company with unstable earnings is likely to pay smaller dividends
(b) Higher tax on dividends leads to lower dividends being paid
(b) Lower tax on dividends allows higher dividends to be declared

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text:
Brightway Group runs three businesses.
(i) In its electrical repair unit, a new trainee works for two years under the guidance of a master electrician before he is allowed to work on his own.
(ii) In its bank, new cashiers are trained in a separate room fitted with the same computers and cash-counting machines as the real counters, so that customers are not affected while the cashiers learn.
(iii) In its engineering firm, final-year engineering students work for eight weeks as part of their degree course, combining practical work with their classroom studies.
Identify the method of training used in each of the three cases.
questions.model:
(i) Apprenticeship training: the trainee works under the guidance of a master worker for a prescribed period to acquire a high level of skill.
(ii) Vestibule training: employees learn their jobs on equipment like that used on the actual job, but in a separate area away from the actual work floor.
(iii) Internship training: a joint programme of training in which educational institutions and business firms cooperate, so that students get practical knowledge along with their studies.

points.t: (i) Apprenticeship training
(ii) Vestibule training
(iii) Internship training

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text:
At Kiran Pharma Ltd., the HR Manager makes sure that workers are not treated differently on the basis of their religion, caste, gender or language, and that all of them are treated with kindliness and justice. The company also avoids frequent transfers: once an employee has been selected and placed after due process, he or she is kept in the post for a reasonable period, so that the employee can settle down and show results.
Identify and explain the two principles of management followed by Kiran Pharma Ltd.
questions.model:
1. Equity: According to Fayol, there should be kindliness and justice in the behaviour of managers towards workers. This ensures loyalty and devotion. There should be no discrimination against anyone on account of sex, religion, language, caste, belief or nationality.
2. Stability of tenure of personnel: Employees, once selected after due process, should be kept at their post for a minimum fixed period. They should have reasonable time to show results. Frequent removal and replacement add to the costs of recruitment, selection and training.

points.t: Identification: Equity
Explanation of equity: kindliness and justice towards workers; no discrimination on grounds of sex, religion, caste, language, etc.
Identification: Stability of tenure of personnel
Explanation of stability of tenure: employees kept in their post for a minimum period to show results; frequent changes increase costs

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: Ritika, the manager of a large hotel, studied the principles of management in a course and has read several books on hotel management. She applies these principles in her own personal way while dealing with guests and staff. Through years of regular practice, she has become very creative in handling difficult situations, and her colleagues say that her style of managing is unique.

parts.q: (a) Identify the nature of management highlighted in the case.

points.t: Management as an art

parts.q: (b) Explain any three features of this nature of management highlighted in the case.
parts.model:
Features of art present in management:
1. Existence of theoretical knowledge: Art presupposes the existence of certain theoretical knowledge. In management there is a lot of literature on its various areas, which a manager can study ('studied the principles of management ... read several books').
2. Personalised application: The use of basic knowledge differs from person to person. A manager applies the acquired knowledge in a personalised manner, and so every manager has his or her own style ('applies these principles in her own personal way').
3. Based on practice and creativity: Art involves the creative use of existing knowledge, and it becomes better with practice. A manager becomes more effective through practice and creativity ('years of regular practice ... very creative').

points.t: First feature: correct heading (any one from the model answer)
First feature: correct explanation of that heading
Second feature: correct heading (any one from the model answer)
Second feature: correct explanation of that heading
Third feature: correct heading (any one from the model answer)
Third feature: correct explanation of that heading

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: Explain any four features of business environment.
questions.model:
Features of business environment (any four):
1. Totality of external forces: Business environment is the sum total of all things external to business firms and, as such, is aggregative in nature.
2. Specific and general forces: Specific forces, such as investors, customers, competitors and suppliers, affect individual firms directly. General forces, such as social, political, legal and technological conditions, affect all firms and only indirectly.
3. Inter-relatedness: The different elements or parts of business environment are closely inter-related. For example, a change in the life expectancy of people increases the demand for health care services.
4. Dynamic nature: Business environment keeps on changing, whether in terms of technology, fashion and tastes of consumers, or government policies.
5. Uncertainty: Business environment is largely uncertain, as it is very difficult to predict future happenings, especially when changes are taking place very fast.
6. Complexity: Business environment consists of many inter-related and dynamic conditions arising from different sources, so it is difficult to understand it in its totality.
7. Relativity: Business environment is a relative concept, since it differs from country to country and even from region to region.

points.t: First feature: correct heading (any one from the model answer)
First feature: correct explanation of that heading
Second feature: correct heading (any one from the model answer)
Second feature: correct explanation of that heading
Third feature: correct heading (any one from the model answer)
Third feature: correct explanation of that heading
Fourth feature: correct heading (any one from the model answer)
Fourth feature: correct explanation of that heading

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text:
The HR Manager of Sunrise Electronics Ltd. took the following steps to motivate the employees:
(i) All employees were given a pension plan and an assurance that their jobs would remain secure.
(ii) Teams were formed and monthly get-togethers were organised, so that employees could make friends at work and feel accepted.
(iii) Outstanding performers were given titles, and their achievements were displayed on the notice board.
(iv) Employees who wished to grow were given challenging assignments that helped them become what they were capable of becoming.
Identify the needs in Maslow's need hierarchy that the HR Manager tried to satisfy through each of these steps.
questions.model:
(i) Safety or security needs: protection from physical and emotional harm, e.g., job security, stability of income, pension plans.
(ii) Affiliation or belonging needs: affection, sense of belongingness, acceptance and friendship.
(iii) Esteem needs: self-respect, autonomy, status, recognition and attention.
(iv) Self-actualisation needs: the drive to become what one is capable of becoming; growth, self-fulfilment and achievement of goals.

points.t: (i) Safety / security needs
(ii) Affiliation / belonging needs
(iii) Esteem needs
(iv) Self-actualisation needs

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text:
Annapurna Bakers set a target that each worker would pack 400 boxes of biscuits in a shift. At the end of every shift, the supervisor recorded the actual number of boxes packed by each worker. On comparing these figures with the target, she found that one worker had packed only 320 boxes. She then found out that this was because the worker's packing machine was old and kept stopping.
Identify and explain the four steps in the process of controlling discussed above.
questions.model:
1. Setting performance standards: Standards are the criteria against which actual performance is measured. They may be set in quantitative or qualitative terms ('pack 400 boxes of biscuits in a shift').
2. Measurement of actual performance: Performance is measured in an objective and reliable manner, for example by personal observation or reports ('recorded the actual number of boxes packed').
3. Comparing actual performance with standards: This reveals the deviation between actual and desired results ('comparing these figures with the target ... only 320 boxes').
4. Analysing deviations: The deviations are checked for their extent and their causes are found, so that suitable corrective action can be taken ('the worker's packing machine was old and kept stopping').

points.t: Setting performance standards, identified
Setting performance standards, explained
Measurement of actual performance, identified
Measurement of actual performance, explained
Comparing actual performance with standards, identified
Comparing actual performance with standards, explained
Analysing deviations, identified
Analysing deviations, explained

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text:
Explain the following functions of marketing:
(a) Standardisation and grading
(b) Customer support services
questions.model:
(a) Standardisation and grading: Standardisation means producing goods of predetermined specifications, which helps in achieving uniformity and consistency in the output. It assures buyers that the goods conform to set standards of quality, price and packaging, and reduces the need for inspection and testing. Grading is the process of classifying products into different groups on the basis of important characteristics such as quality and size. It is especially needed for goods such as agricultural products, and it helps the producer get a higher price for better-quality goods.
(b) Customer support services: Marketers provide services such as after-sales service, handling customer complaints and adjustments, procuring credit services, maintenance services, technical services and consumer information. These services aim at providing maximum satisfaction to customers, which helps in getting repeat sales and in developing brand loyalty.

points.t: (a) Standardisation: producing goods of predetermined specifications to achieve uniformity and consistency
(a) Grading: classifying products into groups on the basis of characteristics such as quality and size
(b) Customer support services named, e.g., after-sales service, handling complaints, credit, maintenance and technical services
(b) Purpose: customer satisfaction, leading to repeat sales and brand loyalty

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: Explain any four limitations of planning.
questions.model:
Limitations of planning (any four):
1. Planning leads to rigidity: Once a well-defined plan is drawn up, managers may not be in a position to change it, even when circumstances change. Sticking rigidly to the plan may not be in the interest of the organisation.
2. Planning may not work in a dynamic environment: The business environment is dynamic and nothing is constant. It is difficult to assess accurately future trends in the economic, political, legal and social dimensions, so plans may fail.
3. Planning reduces creativity: Planning is done by top management and the rest of the organisation just implements the plans. Middle managers and others can neither deviate from plans nor act on their own, so initiative and creativity are discouraged.
4. Planning involves huge costs: Considerable time and money are spent on gathering facts, consulting experts and evaluating alternatives. Sometimes the cost may not justify the benefits.
5. Planning is a time-consuming process: Sometimes so much time is spent on planning that little time is left for implementation.
6. Planning does not guarantee success: Managers may rely on previously tried and tested plans, which may not work again. A plan only gives a direction; success depends on its proper implementation.

points.t: First limitation: correct heading (any one from the model answer)
First limitation: correct explanation of that heading
Second limitation: correct heading (any one from the model answer)
Second limitation: correct explanation of that heading
Third limitation: correct heading (any one from the model answer)
Third limitation: correct explanation of that heading
Fourth limitation: correct heading (any one from the model answer)
Fourth limitation: correct explanation of that heading

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text:
Rajat Sharma, Sales Manager of Swift Appliances Ltd., asked Neha, a sales executive, to take charge of the company's new northern zone. He gave her the right to offer discounts of up to 10% to dealers without asking him. Neha accepted the task of achieving a monthly sales target of ₹25 lakh in the zone. Rajat made it clear that she would have to report the zone's performance to him every week and would be answerable to him for the results.
Identify and explain the three elements of delegation discussed above, quoting the relevant lines.
questions.model:
1. Authority: 'the right to offer discounts of up to 10% to dealers without asking him'. Authority refers to the right of an individual to command subordinates and to take action within the scope of his or her position. It arises from the formal position, flows downward from superior to subordinate, and can be delegated.
2. Responsibility: 'Neha accepted the task of achieving a monthly sales target of ₹25 lakh'. Responsibility is the obligation of a subordinate to properly perform the assigned duty. It arises from the superior-subordinate relationship and flows upward. When authority is delegated, the subordinate becomes responsible, but the superior's responsibility cannot be entirely passed on.
3. Accountability: 'would have to report the zone's performance to him every week and would be answerable to him for the results'. Accountability means answerability for the final outcome. Once authority has been delegated and responsibility accepted, the subordinate is accountable to the superior. It flows upward and cannot be delegated.

points.t: Authority identified
Authority: relevant line quoted
Authority explained: right to command and take decisions; flows downward
Responsibility identified
Responsibility: relevant line quoted
Responsibility explained: obligation to perform the assigned duty; flows upward
Accountability identified
Accountability: relevant line quoted
Accountability explained: answerability for the final outcome; cannot be delegated

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text:
Vardhan Steel Ltd. needs ₹50 crore for a new plant and is deciding how much of it to raise through debt. Its Finance Manager presents the following facts:
(i) Its projected cash flows are large enough to meet interest and loan repayments on time and still leave a sufficient buffer for normal business operations.
(ii) Its earnings before interest and tax are many times its interest charges.
(iii) It earns a return of 18% on its investment, while it can borrow at 10%.
(iv) Its promoters do not want to issue more equity shares, because they fear losing their hold over the management of the company.
Identify and explain the four factors affecting the choice of capital structure discussed above.
questions.model:
1. Cash flow position: The size of projected cash flows must be considered before borrowing. Cash flows must not only cover fixed cash payment obligations such as interest and repayment of principal, but there must also be a sufficient buffer for normal business operations. A company with a strong cash flow position, like Vardhan Steel, can use more debt.
2. Interest coverage ratio (ICR): It refers to the number of times earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) of a company cover its interest obligation. The higher the ratio, the lower the risk of the company failing to meet its interest payments, and the more debt it can use.
3. Return on investment (ROI): If the ROI of the company is higher than the rate of interest on debt, the company can use trading on equity and choose to use more debt to increase its earnings per share. Here ROI (18%) is higher than the cost of debt (10%).
4. Control: Debt normally does not cause a dilution of control, while a public issue of equity may reduce the management's hold on the business. Companies afraid of losing control prefer debt.

points.t: Cash flow position identified
Cash flow position explained: cash flows must cover interest and repayment; strong cash flows allow more debt
Interest coverage ratio identified
Interest coverage ratio explained: number of times EBIT covers interest; higher ratio, more debt can be used
Return on investment identified
Return on investment explained: ROI higher than rate of interest allows more debt (trading on equity)
Control identified
Control explained: debt does not dilute control, while equity may; such companies prefer debt

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: Explain the six rights of a consumer under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
questions.model:
1. Right to safety: The consumer has a right to be protected against goods and services that are hazardous to life, health and property, for example electrical appliances made of poor-quality material. Using ISI-marked products is a safeguard.
2. Right to be informed: The consumer has a right to have complete information about the product, such as its ingredients, date of manufacture, price, quantity and directions for use.
3. Right to be assured (right to choose): The consumer has the right to be assured, wherever possible, of access to a variety of products at competitive prices, so that he or she can choose freely.
4. Right to be heard: The consumer has a right to file a complaint and to be heard in case of dissatisfaction with a good or a service. Many firms have set up consumer service cells for this purpose.
5. Right to seek redressal: The consumer has a right to get relief if the product or service falls short of expectations, for example replacement of the product, removal of the defect or compensation for any loss or injury suffered.
6. Right to consumer education (right to consumer awareness): The consumer has a right to acquire the knowledge needed to be a well-informed consumer throughout life, including knowledge of consumer rights and the remedies available.

points.t: Right to safety, named
Right to safety, explained
Right to be informed, named
Right to be informed, explained
Right to be assured (right to choose), named
Right to be assured (right to choose), explained
Right to be heard, named
Right to be heard, explained
Right to seek redressal, named
Right to seek redressal, explained
Right to consumer education (consumer awareness), named
Right to consumer education (consumer awareness), explained
